items.explanation: Two overlapping current oral anticoagulant orders: apixaban 5 mg BID (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic note documents switching from rivaroxaban to apixaban and starting apixaban, but rivaroxaban was never stopped; the same note still lists both drugs as current. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban confers a high bleeding risk and requires immediate reconciliation.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (absent from the medication list on 2025-12-15, first order authored 2026-03-02). Because the start was on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met (sinus rhythm, QTc ~380 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (first order and first appearance in the medication list). The start is on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. No ECG was obtained inside that window; the only tracing in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and five days after the deadline, so the required monitoring was not completed in time and the due date has passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was restarted at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (it was not on the medication list at the 2026-02-18 visit and the prior inpatient course ended 2026-01-01). The start is on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was restarted at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 after a long gap (previous course ended 2024-09-18). An ECG was therefore required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18, within the required window; the report was requested by fax but has not been received. That outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order authored that day; previous haloperidol exposure was inpatient in early 2025). Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09 (104253928), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily (a new 2026-09-01 warfarin order was also generated). Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD - authorised to adjust warfarin under the standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily for a home INR of 3.4. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review. The home INR of 3.4 pre-dates and triggered the change and cannot satisfy it.

80-year-old woman (born 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented repeatedly in cardiology clinic notes through 2026-06-22. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110, combined systolic/diastolic CHF I5040/I5043), hypertension (I10/4019), age >=75 (2), diabetes mellitus (E119/E11649, on insulin and oral agents), prior stroke/TIA (2 - personal history of TIA/cerebral infarction V1254 and hemiplegia following cerebral infarction I69351), vascular disease (atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery I2510, old myocardial infarction), female sex. There is no anticoagulant on the current medication list - only aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin - and aspirin monotherapy is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Oral anticoagulation is a Class 1 recommendation and should be started unless a contraindication is documented.

71-year-old man (born 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission and carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note through 2026-06-27. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). Score >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but the current medication list contains no anticoagulant (levothyroxine only; INRs around the 2025 admission were 1.1-1.6, consistent with no warfarin). Note the coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' from the same 2025 admission - bleeding risk should be reviewed, but it does not by itself preclude anticoagulation, so this needs a prescriber decision.

71-year-old woman (born 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 2025-03-14, the admission at which she also had cerebral infarction due to embolism (I6340/I639) with residual hemiplegia. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior stroke (2), hypertension (I10/4019, hypertensive CKD I129), age 65-74 (1), female sex (1). Her most recent ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with a PAC, consistent with paroxysmal AF - paroxysmal AF carries the same anticoagulation indication as persistent AF. The current medication list (famotidine, levothyroxine, metoprolol tartrate) contains no anticoagulant and no antithrombotic at all, despite a cardioembolic stroke. Oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated (Class 1).

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is a current order (authored 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04). The outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant was nonetheless re-ordered on 2026-08-20 and no documented cardiology review of the bleed is in the chart, so continuation of apixaban after a major GI bleed needs prescriber review (site treated? PPI? resume vs. switch?). Note the patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk.

48-year-old man (born 1978-02-27) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-07-19 to 2026-08-04 (and 'other specified cardiac dysrhythmias' coded 2025-06-17). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: congestive heart failure (congestive heart failure 4280, acute systolic heart failure 42821 and other primary cardiomyopathies 4254, coded 2025-02-26) plus hypertension (4019/40390). A score of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation. His chart even carries 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' (V5861, 2025-06-17), yet no anticoagulant appears on the current medication list (famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline). Anticoagulation status needs clarification and, if genuinely absent, initiation.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at that encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the note needs correction and the rapid AF needs management review.

Most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT ~490 ms and Bazett QTc ~524 ms, which is >=500 ms and therefore requires prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. The patient has been on escitalopram 10 mg daily continuously since 2024-05-14, with a current order authored 2026-07-18 (valid to 2026-12-26). Most recent electrolytes (2026-03-18) are acceptable: potassium 3.8 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. A repeat ECG on therapy and review of the need for escitalopram are warranted.

Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT ~540 ms and Bazett QTc ~546 ms (>=500 ms), which requires prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (authored 2026-07-12, valid to 2027-01-09) and had been restarted two weeks before that ECG. QTc rose from 424 ms on the prior tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07) to 546 ms after amiodarone was restarted. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so electrolytes do not explain the prolongation.

Most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT ~490 ms and Bazett QTc ~532 ms (>=500 ms), triggering prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. Citalopram 40 mg daily is a current order (authored 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07) and has been refilled continuously since 2023-10-02; 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum recommended when QT prolongation is a concern. Most recent potassium is 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and the most recent magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08), both normal. Dose reduction/alternative agent and a repeat ECG should be considered.

Most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT ~580 ms and Bazett QTc ~571 ms (>=500 ms), requiring prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (authored 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06) and has been continuous outpatient therapy. QTc rose from 467 ms on the prior tracing (100867733, 2022-04-06, atrial fibrillation) to 571 ms after conversion on amiodarone. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17) are normal. This 95-year-old also takes warfarin and metoprolol; an up-to-date ECG and review of continued amiodarone are needed.

Amiodarone (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (it was absent from the medication list at the 2025-09-21 visit and the previous amiodarone course had ended 2025-01-26). Under the 9/1/2025 memo an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG did show QTc ~546 ms, handled as a separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first appearance in the medication list and first order). The start pre-dates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, satisfying the requirement (QTc ~460 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold).

interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07 tracing. Sinus rhythm, rate 81/min with mild rate drift (RR 660-856 ms); upright P in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR ~180 ms. QRS 80 ms with rS in V1 and dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +37 deg (normal). QT ~335 ms, Bazett QTc ~385 ms. No prior ECG in the chart, so no comparison possible. This confirms the same-day note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'.

2025-07-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR ~578 ms), clear upright P in II (0.13 mV) with a normal PR of ~120 ms. QRS 100 ms with rS in V1 - no bundle branch block. Axis +33 deg. QT ~338 ms, Bazett QTc ~444 ms. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 147/min with no identifiable P waves, ST depression and a markedly prolonged repolarisation (QT ~394 ms, QTc ~615 ms). Sinus rhythm has been restored and the QTc has fallen by ~170 ms (>=60 ms).

2024-05-21 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 109/min, regular (RR 540-614 ms), small upright P in II peaking ~130 ms before the QRS with PR ~120 ms. QRS 92 ms - rS in V1, dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block. Axis +47 deg. QT ~328 ms, Bazett QTc ~444 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2026-06-10 19:36 tracing. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (RMSSD ~98 ms, coefficient of variation 0.16), no discernible P waves and a fibrillatory baseline, mean ventricular rate ~144/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 98 ms with rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +7 deg. QT ~290 ms, Bazett QTc ~444 ms. The prior tracing 107914094 from 17:13 the same day is also atrial fibrillation at ~139/min with QTc ~446 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change between them. Note the same-day clinic note records 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict (raised as a separate contradiction item).

2025-08-02 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 69/min, strictly regular (RR 864-884 ms), with a low-amplitude but reproducible P wave (best seen in I/II) giving a PR of ~150 ms. QRS 82 ms - no bundle branch block; qR in I with rS in III/aVF, frontal axis about -26 deg (still within the normal range). QT ~410 ms, Bazett QTc ~439 ms. Prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed sinus rhythm at 60/min, QRS 82 ms, QTc ~411 ms with a markedly different (extreme/right) frontal axis; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc difference 28 ms).

2024-05-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 612-620 ms), upright P in II and aVF peaking ~100 ms before the QRS, PR ~120 ms. QRS 80 ms with rS in V1 and dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis about -3 deg (normal). QT ~308 ms, Bazett QTc ~392 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2025-12-25 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR ~830 ms), upright P in II with PR ~132 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +20 deg. QT ~380 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. This remains the most recent tracing despite escitalopram having been restarted on 2026-08-01 (overdue post-start ECG raised separately).

2024-11-15 tracing. Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (RMSSD ~287 ms, coefficient of variation 0.20), no organised P waves (residual atrial deflection only 0.05 mV on the signal-averaged beat), mean ventricular rate ~53/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 90 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis +23 deg. QT ~446 ms, Bazett QTc ~419 ms. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear 0.27 mV P wave and PR ~160 ms, QTc ~394 ms - so atrial fibrillation is new since that tracing; QTc is unchanged (25 ms).

2025-03-09 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 58/min (mild sinus bradycardia), regular, prominent upright P in II (0.25 mV) with PR ~105 ms. QRS 90 ms, rS in V1 and dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +59 deg. QT ~435 ms, Bazett QTc ~429 ms. Prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08) was essentially identical (sinus 62/min, QRS 88 ms, QTc ~447 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

2025-08-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular (RR ~720 ms), upright P in II with PR ~136 ms. QRS 78 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +55 deg. QT ~341 ms, Bazett QTc ~402 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2020-06-19 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular, upright P in II (0.28 mV) with PR ~146 ms. QRS 74 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +57 deg. Repolarisation is prolonged with a long, low T-wave tail: QT ~445 ms, Bazett QTc ~505 ms. The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) showed sinus rhythm at 75/min, QRS 92 ms and a similarly prolonged QT (~477 ms, QTc ~532 ms); measured the same way the QTc change is under 60 ms, so no QTc change is flagged. The patient is not currently on any QT watch-list drug.

2021-01-18 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 120/min (RR 496-504 ms) with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR ~180 ms. QRS 96 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no conduction block. Axis +65 deg (normal). QT ~277 ms, QTc ~392 ms. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc ~398 ms) the rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc difference 6 ms).

2025-06-23 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 54/min, regular, with a clearly visible P wave in II/aVF beginning ~255 ms before the QRS: PR ~215 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 86 ms with an rSr' in V1 that is not wide enough for right bundle branch block and a tall R in V6. Axis +14 deg. QT ~398 ms, Bazett QTc ~379 ms. Prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) was sinus at 51/min with a PR of ~185 ms, QRS 88 ms and QTc ~359 ms: no bundle branch block change and QTc unchanged (20 ms); the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree block range.

2025-09-13 tracing. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: RR intervals range 288-580 ms in a chaotic pattern (RMSSD ~104 ms), with no organised P wave anywhere and a flat/fibrillatory baseline; mean ventricular rate ~152/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis -15 deg. QT ~255 ms, Bazett QTc ~407 ms. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at ~77/min (regular RR ~780 ms apart from one ectopic beat) with a small but definite P wave and PR ~150 ms, QTc ~409 ms. Atrial fibrillation is therefore new; QTc is unchanged.

2025-11-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 73/min, regular, prominent upright P in II (0.25 mV) with PR ~165 ms. QRS 94 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +2 deg. QT ~356 ms, Bazett QTc ~394 ms. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was also sinus rhythm (67/min, QRS 92 ms) but with a much longer QT (~500 ms, QTc ~528 ms); the QTc has fallen by ~134 ms (>=60 ms). This tracing confirms the same-day note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'.

2025-02-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular (RR ~810 ms), well-formed upright P in II with PR ~176 ms (normal, below the 200 ms first-degree block threshold). QRS 92 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis +66 deg. QT ~378 ms, Bazett QTc ~420 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2023-06-26 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, strictly regular (RR 536-542 ms), with a single well-formed upright P wave in II (0.19 mV) per cycle beginning ~200 ms before the QRS: PR ~160 ms, 1:1 atrial-ventricular relationship, i.e. not atrial flutter despite the flutter coded elsewhere in the chart. QRS 98 ms with a very deep S in V1 (-3.0 mV) and tall R in I/V6 - LVH voltage, no bundle branch block. Axis +31 deg. QT ~294 ms, Bazett QTc ~401 ms. Prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) was identical in rhythm and conduction (sinus 115/min, QRS 96 ms, QTc ~393 ms): no change.

2025-03-14 tracing. Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min: the RR intervals are ~980 ms apart from a single early beat (538 ms) with a compensatory pause (1372 ms), i.e. one atrial ectopic, and a broad low-amplitude upright P wave precedes each sinus QRS starting ~250 ms before it - PR ~205 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. This is not atrial fibrillation, which fits the 'paroxysmal' atrial fibrillation coded at this encounter. QRS 100 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -33 deg (left axis deviation). QT ~390 ms, Bazett QTc ~394 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2026-04-29 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular (RR ~870 ms), upright P in II with PR ~134 ms. QRS 94 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. The QRS is deeply negative in I (S -1.3 mV) with a negative net aVF, giving a frontal axis of about -171 deg (extreme axis deviation). QT ~353 ms, Bazett QTc ~380 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2023-11-10 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, upright P in II with PR ~144 ms. QRS 102 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis +41 deg. Repolarisation is prolonged: QT ~490 ms, Bazett QTc ~532 ms. The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) showed sinus tachycardia at 132/min with QRS 96 ms and QTc ~436 ms; QTc has increased by ~96 ms (>=60 ms). The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug - flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2026-03-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR ~880 ms), upright P in II with PR ~144 ms. QRS 88 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +44 deg. The T wave is biphasic (negative then positive in V5/II) and ends late: QT ~440-450 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 470 ms - prolonged but below the 500 ms threshold that would mandate prescriber review, so no QT safety item was raised. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. This is the post-start ECG for escitalopram begun 2026-02-12.

2019-01-13 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, upright P in II (0.23 mV) with PR ~168 ms. QRS 92 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis about -14 deg (normal). QT ~382 ms, Bazett QTc ~359 ms. Prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) was sinus at 66/min with PR ~190 ms, QRS 106 ms and QTc ~390 ms: no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (31 ms).

2023-10-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, upright P in II, PR ~130 ms, QRS 92 ms (rS V1, tall R V6, no BBB), axis +35 deg. The T wave is markedly prolonged: QT ~490 ms, Bazett QTc ~524 ms. Prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) had identical rhythm/conduction but QT ~325 ms and QTc ~364 ms, so QTc has increased by ~160 ms (>=60 ms). The patient is on escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug - flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2022-07-13 tracing. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141/min (RR 404-454 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02). No sinus P wave: the deflection 170 ms before each QRS is negative in II, III and aVF and positive in V1 - the classic typical (counter-clockwise) flutter wave vector - and recurs at ~210 ms intervals, i.e. an atrial rate of ~280/min conducted 2:1, with the alternate flutter wave buried in the QRS. For comparison, this patient's sinus tracings show an upright 0.08 mV P wave in II, which is absent here. No measurable PR interval in flutter. QRS 86 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis -7 deg. QT ~280 ms, Bazett QTc ~429 ms. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) was atrial fibrillation (RR 380-822 ms, RMSSD ~190 ms, no organised atrial activity) at ~110/min with QTc ~432 ms, so the atrial fibrillation has organised into atrial flutter; QTc unchanged. No pacing spikes are seen despite the documented pacemaker.

2025-05-12 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (RR ~730 ms), upright P in II with PR ~138 ms. QRS 104 ms - slightly widened but below 120 ms and without an rSR' in V1 or a broad monophasic R in V6, so no bundle branch block. Axis +28 deg. QT ~371 ms, Bazett QTc ~435 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2022-07-16 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 91/min, regular, upright P in II with PR ~154 ms. QRS 82 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -52 deg (left axis deviation, qR in I with rS in II/III/aVF). QT ~337 ms, Bazett QTc ~415 ms. Prior ECG 102616671 (2021-05-16) was sinus at 87/min, QRS 86 ms, QTc ~397 ms with a +21 deg axis: rhythm, conduction and QTc unchanged (18 ms); only the frontal axis has shifted leftward.

2024-07-17 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 61/min with a broad P wave in II starting ~275 ms before the QRS: PR ~210 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS is wide at 134 ms with a deep, slurred QS/rS complex in V1 (nadir -1.4 mV) and a broad notched monophasic R in I and V6 peaking late (~120 ms after QRS onset) with no S wave - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -25 deg. QT ~456 ms, Bazett QTc ~460 ms. Prior ECG 103686933 (2024-06-03) showed the same pattern (sinus 68/min, PR ~212 ms, QRS 132 ms LBBB, QTc ~462 ms), so there is no new or resolved block and no QTc change.

2025-03-19 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular (RR ~590 ms), prominent upright P in II with PR ~134 ms. QRS 92 ms; V1 shows a dominant late R with only a small S, but the QRS is narrow so this is not right bundle branch block. Axis +43 deg. QT ~337 ms, Bazett QTc ~439 ms. Prior ECG 101016166 (2025-03-18) was essentially identical (sinus 102/min, QRS 88 ms, QTc ~436 ms): no change.

2025-09-22 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 66/min, regular (RR ~910 ms), upright P in II with PR ~148 ms. QRS 98 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -27 deg, at the lower edge of normal. QT ~375 ms, Bazett QTc ~393 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2022-04-27 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 58/min, essentially regular, with an upright P wave in II beginning ~220 ms before each QRS: PR ~174 ms. QRS 90 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis +34 deg. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT ~580 ms, Bazett QTc ~571 ms. The prior ECG 100867733 (2022-04-06) was atrial fibrillation (RR 324-616 ms, RMSSD ~136 ms, no atrial activity) at ~131/min with QTc ~467 ms. Sinus rhythm has therefore been restored and the QTc has risen by ~104 ms (>=60 ms) - consistent with amiodarone, a QT watch-list drug, which is raised separately as a QT safety item.

2022-05-01 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 107/min, regular (RR ~560 ms), upright P in II with PR ~150 ms. QRS 76 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +43 deg. QT ~320 ms, Bazett QTc ~428 ms. Prior ECG 107274479 (2019-07-27) was sinus at 75/min, QRS 76 ms, QTc ~417 ms: no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (11 ms).

2024-04-19 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121/min (RR 492-500 ms), upright P in II/aVF before every QRS, PR ~125 ms. QRS 86 ms with rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +68 deg (normal). QT ~296 ms, Bazett QTc ~421 ms (upper normal, largely a consequence of Bazett over-correction at this rate). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior for comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, regular, upright P in II with PR ~130 ms. QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 (-1.07 mV) with tall R in V6 - voltage criteria only, no BBB. Axis +54 deg. QT ~317 ms, QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier and is essentially identical (101/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~409 ms): no change.

2024-10-24 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), broad low-amplitude but consistent P wave in II, PR ~160 ms. QRS 92 ms with rS in V1 and very tall R in V6 (3.3 mV, LVH voltage). Axis +34 deg. QT ~430 ms, QTc ~401 ms. arguments.explanation: 2022-07-13 tracing. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141/min (RR 404-454 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02). No sinus P wave: the deflection 170 ms before each QRS is negative in II, III and aVF and positive in V1 - the classic typical (counter-clockwise) flutter wave vector - and recurs at ~210 ms intervals, i.e. an atrial rate of ~280/min conducted 2:1, with the alternate flutter wave buried in the QRS. For comparison, this patient's sinus tracings show an upright 0.08 mV P wave in II, which is absent here. No measurable PR interval in flutter. QRS 86 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis -7 deg. QT ~280 ms, Bazett QTc ~429 ms. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) was atrial fibrillation (RR 380-822 ms, RMSSD ~190 ms, no organised atrial activity) at ~110/min with QTc ~432 ms, so the atrial fibrillation has organised into atrial flutter; QTc unchanged. No pacing spikes are seen despite the documented pacemaker.

2025-07-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR ~578 ms), clear upright P in II (0.13 mV) with a normal PR of ~120 ms. QRS 100 ms with rS in V1 - no bundle branch block. Axis +33 deg. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 147/min with no identifiable P waves, ST depression and a markedly prolonged repolarisation (QT ~394 ms, QTc ~615 ms). 2024-05-21 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 109/min, regular (RR 540-614 ms), small upright P in II peaking ~130 ms before the QRS with PR ~120 ms. 2021-01-18 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 120/min (RR 496-504 ms) with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR ~180 ms. QRS 96 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no conduction block. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc ~398 ms) the rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc difference 6 ms).

2023-10-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, upright P in II, PR ~130 ms, QRS 92 ms (rS V1, tall R V6, no BBB), axis +35 deg. The T wave is markedly prolonged: QT ~490 ms, Bazett QTc ~524 ms. Prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) had identical rhythm/conduction but QT ~325 ms and QTc ~364 ms, so QTc has increased by ~160 ms (>=60 ms). The patient is on escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug - flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2024-04-19 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121/min (RR 492-500 ms), upright P in II/aVF before every QRS, PR ~125 ms. QRS 86 ms with rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +68 deg (normal). QT ~296 ms, Bazett QTc ~421 ms (upper normal, largely a consequence of Bazett over-correction at this rate). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior for comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, regular, upright P in II with PR ~130 ms. QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 (-1.07 mV) with tall R in V6 - voltage criteria only, no BBB. Axis +54 deg. QT ~317 ms, QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier and is essentially identical (101/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~409 ms): no change.

2024-10-24 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), broad low-amplitude but consistent P wave in II, PR ~160 ms. QRS 92 ms with rS in V1 and very tall R in V6 (3.3 mV, LVH voltage). Axis +34 deg. QT ~430 ms, QTc ~401 ms. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus rhythm 57/min with one ectopic beat, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~404 ms - no interval or rhythm change. Of note, sinus rhythm here despite atrial fibrillation and Mobitz II being coded at this encounter; no AV block is evident on this tracing.

2024-12-05 14:38 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121/min (RR 492-496 ms), P wave before each QRS, PR ~100 ms. QRS is now narrow at 98 ms. The QRS is predominantly negative in I with an almost isoelectric, slightly negative aVF, giving a frontal axis of about -178 deg (extreme axis deviation). QT ~296 ms, QTc ~421 ms. The prior ECG 106516875 from earlier the same day (01:33) showed a QRS of ~150-158 ms with an rSR' pattern and a tall late R in V1 (1.14 mV peaking 114 ms after QRS onset) plus broad terminal S in I/V6 - right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day. That block has resolved on the later tracing (QTc 476 -> 421 ms, a 55 ms fall, below the 60 ms threshold).

2025-11-24 tracing. Sinus rhythm 62/min, regular, P wave in II with PR ~165 ms. QRS 100 ms, rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no BBB. Axis +64 deg. Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT ~540 ms, Bazett QTc ~546 ms. Prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) showed sinus rhythm with sinus arrhythmia at 47/min, QRS 100 ms, QT ~478 ms and QTc ~424 ms; QTc has therefore risen by ~120 ms (>=60 ms), coinciding with amiodarone being restarted on 2025-11-10. Flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2024-09-17 tracing. Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 386-1070 ms, RMSSD ~254 ms) with no organised or reproducible P wave in any lead, mean ventricular rate ~99/min. Because there is no atrial activity, no PR interval is measurable. QRS 84 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -63 deg (left axis deviation). QT ~324 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; atrial fibrillation was coded at the preceding day's encounter.

2025-07-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR ~578 ms), clear upright P in II (0.13 mV) with a normal PR of ~120 ms. QRS 100 ms with rS in V1 - no bundle branch block. Axis +33 deg. 2024-05-21 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 109/min, regular (RR 540-614 ms), small upright P in II peaking ~130 ms before the QRS with PR ~120 ms. 2026-06-10 19:36 tracing. Prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed sinus rhythm at 60/min, QRS 82 ms, QTc ~411 ms with a markedly different (extreme/right) frontal axis; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc difference 28 ms).

2024-05-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 612-620 ms), upright P in II and aVF peaking ~100 ms before the QRS, PR ~120 ms. 2025-12-25 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR ~830 ms), upright P in II with PR ~132 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +20 deg. 2024-11-15 tracing. 2021-01-18 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 120/min (RR 496-504 ms) with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR ~180 ms. QRS 96 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no conduction block. 2023-10-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, upright P in II, PR ~130 ms, QRS 92 ms (rS V1, tall R V6, no BBB), axis +35 deg. The T wave is markedly prolonged: QT ~490 ms, Bazett QTc ~524 ms. 2024-04-19 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121/min (RR 492-500 ms), upright P in II/aVF before every QRS, PR ~125 ms. QRS 86 ms with rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +68 deg (normal). QT ~296 ms, Bazett QTc ~421 ms (upper normal, largely a consequence of Bazett over-correction at this rate). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior for comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, regular, upright P in II with PR ~130 ms. QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 (-1.07 mV) with tall R in V6 - voltage criteria only, no BBB. Axis +54 deg. QT ~317 ms, QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier and is essentially identical (101/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~409 ms): no change.

2024-10-24 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), broad low-amplitude but consistent P wave in II, PR ~160 ms. QRS 92 ms with rS in V1 and very tall R in V6 (3.3 mV, LVH voltage). Axis +34 deg. QT ~430 ms, QTc ~401 ms. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus rhythm 57/min with one ectopic beat, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~404 ms - no interval or rhythm change. Of note, sinus rhythm here despite atrial fibrillation and Mobitz II being coded at this encounter; no AV block is evident on this tracing.

The QRS is predominantly negative in I with an almost isoelectric, slightly negative aVF, giving a frontal axis of about -178 deg (extreme axis deviation). QT ~296 ms, QTc ~421 ms. The prior ECG 106516875 from earlier the same day (01:33) showed a QRS of ~150-158 ms with an rSR' pattern and a tall late R in V1 (1.14 mV peaking 114 ms after QRS onset) plus broad terminal S in I/V6 - right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day. That block has resolved on the later tracing (QTc 476 -> 421 ms, a 55 ms fall, below the 60 ms threshold).

2025-11-24 tracing. Sinus rhythm 62/min, regular, P wave in II with PR ~165 ms. QRS 100 ms, rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no BBB. Axis +64 deg. Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT ~540 ms, Bazett QTc ~546 ms. Prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) showed sinus rhythm with sinus arrhythmia at 47/min, QRS 100 ms, QT ~478 ms and QTc ~424 ms; QTc has therefore risen by ~120 ms (>=60 ms), coinciding with amiodarone being restarted on 2025-11-10. Flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2024-09-17 tracing. Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 386-1070 ms, RMSSD ~254 ms) with no organised or reproducible P wave in any lead, mean ventricular rate ~99/min. Because there is no atrial activity, no PR interval is measurable. QRS 84 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -63 deg (left axis deviation). QT ~324 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; atrial fibrillation was coded at the preceding day's encounter.

interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07 tracing. Sinus rhythm, rate 81/min with mild rate drift (RR 660-856 ms); upright P in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR ~180 ms. QRS 80 ms with rS in V1 and dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +37 deg (normal). QT ~335 ms, Bazett QTc ~385 ms. No prior ECG in the chart, so no comparison possible. This confirms the same-day note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'.

2025-07-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR ~578 ms), clear upright P in II (0.13 mV) with a normal PR of ~120 ms. QRS 100 ms with rS in V1 - no bundle branch block. Axis +33 deg. QT ~338 ms, Bazett QTc ~444 ms. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 147/min with no identifiable P waves, ST depression and a markedly prolonged repolarisation (QT ~394 ms, QTc ~615 ms). Sinus rhythm has been restored and the QTc has fallen by ~170 ms (>=60 ms).

2024-05-21 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 109/min, regular (RR 540-614 ms), small upright P in II peaking ~130 ms before the QRS with PR ~120 ms. 2026-06-10 19:36 tracing. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (RMSSD ~98 ms, coefficient of variation 0.16), no discernible P waves and a fibrillatory baseline, mean ventricular rate ~144/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 98 ms with rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +7 deg. QT ~290 ms, Bazett QTc ~444 ms. The prior tracing 107914094 from 17:13 the same day is also atrial fibrillation at ~139/min with QTc ~446 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change between them. Note the same-day clinic note records 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict (raised as a separate contradiction item).

2025-08-02 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 69/min, strictly regular (RR 864-884 ms), with a low-amplitude but reproducible P wave (best seen in I/II) giving a PR of ~150 ms. Prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed sinus rhythm at 60/min, QRS 82 ms, QTc ~411 ms with a markedly different (extreme/right) frontal axis; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc difference 28 ms).

2024-05-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 612-620 ms), upright P in II and aVF peaking ~100 ms before the QRS, PR ~120 ms. 2025-12-25 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR ~830 ms), upright P in II with PR ~132 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +20 deg. QT ~380 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. This remains the most recent tracing despite escitalopram having been restarted on 2026-08-01 (overdue post-start ECG raised separately).

2024-11-15 tracing. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear 0.27 mV P wave and PR ~160 ms, QTc ~394 ms - so atrial fibrillation is new since that tracing; QTc is unchanged (25 ms).

2025-08-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular (RR ~720 ms), upright P in II with PR ~136 ms. QRS 78 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +55 deg. QT ~341 ms, Bazett QTc ~402 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2020-06-19 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular, upright P in II (0.28 mV) with PR ~146 ms. QRS 74 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +57 deg. The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) showed sinus rhythm at 75/min, QRS 92 ms and a similarly prolonged QT (~477 ms, QTc ~532 ms); measured the same way the QTc change is under 60 ms, so no QTc change is flagged. 2021-01-18 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 120/min (RR 496-504 ms) with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR ~180 ms. QRS 96 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no conduction block. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc ~398 ms) the rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc difference 6 ms).

2023-10-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, upright P in II, PR ~130 ms, QRS 92 ms (rS V1, tall R V6, no BBB), axis +35 deg. The T wave is markedly prolonged: QT ~490 ms, Bazett QTc ~524 ms. Prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) had identical rhythm/conduction but QT ~325 ms and QTc ~364 ms, so QTc has increased by ~160 ms (>=60 ms). The patient is on escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug - flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2024-04-19 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121/min (RR 492-500 ms), upright P in II/aVF before every QRS, PR ~125 ms. QRS 86 ms with rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +68 deg (normal). QT ~296 ms, Bazett QTc ~421 ms (upper normal, largely a consequence of Bazett over-correction at this rate). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior for comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, regular, upright P in II with PR ~130 ms. QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 (-1.07 mV) with tall R in V6 - voltage criteria only, no BBB. Axis +54 deg. QT ~317 ms, QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier and is essentially identical (101/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~409 ms): no change.

2024-10-24 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), broad low-amplitude but consistent P wave in II, PR ~160 ms. QRS 92 ms with rS in V1 and very tall R in V6 (3.3 mV, LVH voltage). Axis +34 deg. QT ~430 ms, QTc ~401 ms. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus rhythm 57/min with one ectopic beat, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~404 ms - no interval or rhythm change. Of note, sinus rhythm here despite atrial fibrillation and Mobitz II being coded at this encounter; no AV block is evident on this tracing.

2024-12-05 14:38 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121/min (RR 492-496 ms), P wave before each QRS, PR ~100 ms. QRS is now narrow at 98 ms. The prior ECG 106516875 from earlier the same day (01:33) showed a QRS of ~150-158 ms with an rSR' pattern and a tall late R in V1 (1.14 mV peaking 114 ms after QRS onset) plus broad terminal S in I/V6 - right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day. That block has resolved on the later tracing (QTc 476 -> 421 ms, a 55 ms fall, below the 60 ms threshold).

2025-11-24 tracing. Sinus rhythm 62/min, regular, P wave in II with PR ~165 ms. QRS 100 ms, rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no BBB. Axis +64 deg. Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT ~540 ms, Bazett QTc ~546 ms. Prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) showed sinus rhythm with sinus arrhythmia at 47/min, QRS 100 ms, QT ~478 ms and QTc ~424 ms; QTc has therefore risen by ~120 ms (>=60 ms), coinciding with amiodarone being restarted on 2025-11-10. Flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2024-09-17 tracing. Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 386-1070 ms, RMSSD ~254 ms) with no organised or reproducible P wave in any lead, mean ventricular rate ~99/min. Because there is no atrial activity, no PR interval is measurable. QRS 84 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -63 deg (left axis deviation). QT ~324 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; atrial fibrillation was coded at the preceding day's encounter.

80-year-old woman (born 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented repeatedly in cardiology clinic notes through 2026-06-22. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110, combined systolic/diastolic CHF I5040/I5043), hypertension (I10/4019), age >=75 (2), diabetes mellitus (E119/E11649, on insulin and oral agents), prior stroke/TIA (2 - personal history of TIA/cerebral infarction V1254 and hemiplegia following cerebral infarction I69351), vascular disease (atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery I2510, old myocardial infarction), female sex. There is no anticoagulant on the current medication list - only aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin - and aspirin monotherapy is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Oral anticoagulation is a Class 1 recommendation and should be started unless a contraindication is documented.

71-year-old man (born 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission and carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note through 2026-06-27. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). Score >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but the current medication list contains no anticoagulant (levothyroxine only; INRs around the 2025 admission were 1.1-1.6, consistent with no warfarin). Note the coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' from the same 2025 admission - bleeding risk should be reviewed, but it does not by itself preclude anticoagulation, so this needs a prescriber decision.

71-year-old woman (born 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 2025-03-14, the admission at which she also had cerebral infarction due to embolism (I6340/I639) with residual hemiplegia. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior stroke (2), hypertension (I10/4019, hypertensive CKD I129), age 65-74 (1), female sex (1). Her most recent ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with a PAC, consistent with paroxysmal AF - paroxysmal AF carries the same anticoagulation indication as persistent AF. The current medication list (famotidine, levothyroxine, metoprolol tartrate) contains no anticoagulant and no antithrombotic at all, despite a cardioembolic stroke. Oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated (Class 1).

PPI? resume vs. switch?). Note the patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk.

48-year-old man (born 1978-02-27) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-07-19 to 2026-08-04 (and 'other specified cardiac dysrhythmias' coded 2025-06-17). His chart even carries 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' (V5861, 2025-06-17), yet no anticoagulant appears on the current medication list (famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline). Anticoagulation status needs clarification and, if genuinely absent, initiation.

interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07 tracing. Sinus rhythm, rate 81/min with mild rate drift (RR 660-856 ms); upright P in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR ~180 ms. QRS 80 ms with rS in V1 and dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +37 deg (normal). QT ~335 ms, Bazett QTc ~385 ms. No prior ECG in the chart, so no comparison possible. 2025-07-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR ~578 ms), clear upright P in II (0.13 mV) with a normal PR of ~120 ms. QRS 100 ms with rS in V1 - no bundle branch block. Axis +33 deg. QT ~338 ms, Bazett QTc ~444 ms. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 147/min with no identifiable P waves, ST depression and a markedly prolonged repolarisation (QT ~394 ms, QTc ~615 ms). Sinus rhythm has been restored and the QTc has fallen by ~170 ms (>=60 ms).

2024-05-21 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 109/min, regular (RR 540-614 ms), small upright P in II peaking ~130 ms before the QRS with PR ~120 ms. QRS 92 ms - rS in V1, dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block. Axis +47 deg. QT ~328 ms, Bazett QTc ~444 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2026-06-10 19:36 tracing. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (RMSSD ~98 ms, coefficient of variation 0.16), no discernible P waves and a fibrillatory baseline, mean ventricular rate ~144/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 98 ms with rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +7 deg. QT ~290 ms, Bazett QTc ~444 ms. The prior tracing 107914094 from 17:13 the same day is also atrial fibrillation at ~139/min with QTc ~446 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change between them. Note the same-day clinic note records 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which these tracings contradict (raised as a separate contradiction item).

2025-08-02 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 69/min, strictly regular (RR 864-884 ms), with a low-amplitude but reproducible P wave (best seen in I/II) giving a PR of ~150 ms. QRS 82 ms - no bundle branch block; qR in I with rS in III/aVF, frontal axis about -26 deg (still within the normal range). QT ~410 ms, Bazett QTc ~439 ms. Prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed sinus rhythm at 60/min, QRS 82 ms, QTc ~411 ms with a markedly different (extreme/right) frontal axis; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc difference 28 ms).

2024-05-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 612-620 ms), upright P in II and aVF peaking ~100 ms before the QRS, PR ~120 ms. QRS 80 ms with rS in V1 and dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis about -3 deg (normal). QT ~308 ms, Bazett QTc ~392 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2025-12-25 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR ~830 ms), upright P in II with PR ~132 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +20 deg. QT ~380 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. This remains the most recent tracing despite escitalopram having been restarted on 2026-08-01 (overdue post-start ECG raised separately).

2024-11-15 tracing. Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (RMSSD ~287 ms, coefficient of variation 0.20), no organised P waves (residual atrial deflection only 0.05 mV on the signal-averaged beat), mean ventricular rate ~53/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 90 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis +23 deg. QT ~446 ms, Bazett QTc ~419 ms. The prior ECG 107873952 (2024-11-12) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear 0.27 mV P wave and PR ~160 ms, QTc ~394 ms - so atrial fibrillation is new since that tracing; QTc is unchanged (25 ms).

2025-03-09 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 58/min (mild sinus bradycardia), regular, prominent upright P in II (0.25 mV) with PR ~105 ms. QRS 90 ms, rS in V1 and dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +59 deg. QT ~435 ms, Bazett QTc ~429 ms. Prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08) was essentially identical (sinus 62/min, QRS 88 ms, QTc ~447 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

2025-08-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular (RR ~720 ms), upright P in II with PR ~136 ms. QRS 78 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +55 deg. QT ~341 ms, Bazett QTc ~402 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2020-06-19 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular, upright P in II (0.28 mV) with PR ~146 ms. QRS 74 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +57 deg. Repolarisation is prolonged with a long, low T-wave tail: QT ~445 ms, Bazett QTc ~505 ms. The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) showed sinus rhythm at 75/min, QRS 92 ms and a similarly prolonged QT (~477 ms, QTc ~532 ms); measured the same way the QTc change is under 60 ms, so no QTc change is flagged. The patient is not currently on any QT watch-list drug.

2021-01-18 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 120/min (RR 496-504 ms) with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR ~180 ms. QRS 96 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no conduction block. Axis +65 deg (normal). QT ~277 ms, QTc ~392 ms. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc ~398 ms) the rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc difference 6 ms).

2025-06-23 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 54/min, regular, with a clearly visible P wave in II/aVF beginning ~255 ms before the QRS: PR ~215 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 86 ms with an rSr' in V1 that is not wide enough for right bundle branch block and a tall R in V6. Axis +14 deg. QT ~398 ms, Bazett QTc ~379 ms. Prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) was sinus at 51/min with a PR of ~185 ms, QRS 88 ms and QTc ~359 ms: no bundle branch block change and QTc unchanged (20 ms); the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree block range.

2025-09-13 tracing. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: RR intervals range 288-580 ms in a chaotic pattern (RMSSD ~104 ms), with no organised P wave anywhere and a flat/fibrillatory baseline; mean ventricular rate ~152/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis -15 deg. QT ~255 ms, Bazett QTc ~407 ms. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at ~77/min (regular RR ~780 ms apart from one ectopic beat) with a small but definite P wave and PR ~150 ms, QTc ~409 ms. Atrial fibrillation is therefore new; QTc is unchanged.

2023-10-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, upright P in II, PR ~130 ms, QRS 92 ms (rS V1, tall R V6, no BBB), axis +35 deg. The T wave is markedly prolonged: QT ~490 ms, Bazett QTc ~524 ms. Prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) had identical rhythm/conduction but QT ~325 ms and QTc ~364 ms, so QTc has increased by ~160 ms (>=60 ms). The patient is on escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug - flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2024-04-19 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121/min (RR 492-500 ms), upright P in II/aVF before every QRS, PR ~125 ms. QRS 86 ms with rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +68 deg (normal). QT ~296 ms, Bazett QTc ~421 ms (upper normal, largely a consequence of Bazett over-correction at this rate). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior for comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, regular, upright P in II with PR ~130 ms. QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 (-1.07 mV) with tall R in V6 - voltage criteria only, no BBB. Axis +54 deg. QT ~317 ms, QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier and is essentially identical (101/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~409 ms): no change.

2024-10-24 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), broad low-amplitude but consistent P wave in II, PR ~160 ms. QRS 92 ms with rS in V1 and very tall R in V6 (3.3 mV, LVH voltage). Axis +34 deg. QT ~430 ms, QTc ~401 ms. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus rhythm 57/min with one ectopic beat, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~404 ms - no interval or rhythm change. Of note, sinus rhythm here despite atrial fibrillation and Mobitz II being coded at this encounter; no AV block is evident on this tracing.

2024-12-05 14:38 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121/min (RR 492-496 ms), P wave before each QRS, PR ~100 ms. QRS is now narrow at 98 ms. The QRS is predominantly negative in I with an almost isoelectric, slightly negative aVF, giving a frontal axis of about -178 deg (extreme axis deviation). QT ~296 ms, QTc ~421 ms. The prior ECG 106516875 from earlier the same day (01:33) showed a QRS of ~150-158 ms with an rSR' pattern and a tall late R in V1 (1.14 mV peaking 114 ms after QRS onset) plus broad terminal S in I/V6 - right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day. That block has resolved on the later tracing (QTc 476 -> 421 ms, a 55 ms fall, below the 60 ms threshold).

2025-11-24 tracing. Sinus rhythm 62/min, regular, P wave in II with PR ~165 ms. QRS 100 ms, rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no BBB. Axis +64 deg. Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT ~540 ms, Bazett QTc ~546 ms. Prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) showed sinus rhythm with sinus arrhythmia at 47/min, QRS 100 ms, QT ~478 ms and QTc ~424 ms; QTc has therefore risen by ~120 ms (>=60 ms), coinciding with amiodarone being restarted on 2025-11-10. Flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2024-09-17 tracing. Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 386-1070 ms, RMSSD ~254 ms) with no organised or reproducible P wave in any lead, mean ventricular rate ~99/min. Because there is no atrial activity, no PR interval is measurable. QRS 84 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -63 deg (left axis deviation). QT ~324 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; atrial fibrillation was coded at the preceding day's encounter.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110, combined systolic/diastolic CHF I5040/I5043), hypertension (I10/4019), age >=75 (2), diabetes mellitus (E119/E11649, on insulin and oral agents), prior stroke/TIA (2 - personal history of TIA/cerebral infarction V1254 and hemiplegia following cerebral infarction I69351), vascular disease (atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery I2510, old myocardial infarction), female sex. There is no anticoagulant on the current medication list - only aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin - and aspirin monotherapy is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Oral anticoagulation is a Class 1 recommendation and should be started unless a contraindication is documented.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). Note the coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' from the same 2025 admission - bleeding risk should be reviewed, but it does not by itself preclude anticoagulation, so this needs a prescriber decision.

Oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated (Class 1).

Anticoagulation status needs clarification and, if genuinely absent, initiation.

interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07 tracing. Sinus rhythm, rate 81/min with mild rate drift (RR 660-856 ms); upright P in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR ~180 ms. QRS 80 ms with rS in V1 and dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +37 deg (normal). QT ~335 ms, Bazett QTc ~385 ms. No prior ECG in the chart, so no comparison possible. This confirms the same-day note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'.

2025-07-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR ~578 ms), clear upright P in II (0.13 mV) with a normal PR of ~120 ms. QRS 100 ms with rS in V1 - no bundle branch block. Axis +33 deg. QT ~338 ms, Bazett QTc ~444 ms. The prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 147/min with no identifiable P waves, ST depression and a markedly prolonged repolarisation (QT ~394 ms, QTc ~615 ms). 2024-05-21 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 109/min, regular (RR 540-614 ms), small upright P in II peaking ~130 ms before the QRS with PR ~120 ms. QRS 92 ms - rS in V1, dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block. Axis +47 deg. QT ~328 ms, Bazett QTc ~444 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2026-06-10 19:36 tracing. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (RMSSD ~98 ms, coefficient of variation 0.16), no discernible P waves and a fibrillatory baseline, mean ventricular rate ~144/min. 2024-05-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 612-620 ms), upright P in II and aVF peaking ~100 ms before the QRS, PR ~120 ms. 2025-12-25 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR ~830 ms), upright P in II with PR ~132 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +20 deg. 2025-08-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular (RR ~720 ms), upright P in II with PR ~136 ms. QRS 78 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +55 deg. QT ~341 ms, Bazett QTc ~402 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2020-06-19 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular, upright P in II (0.28 mV) with PR ~146 ms. QRS 74 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +57 deg. Repolarisation is prolonged with a long, low T-wave tail: QT ~445 ms, Bazett QTc ~505 ms. The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) showed sinus rhythm at 75/min, QRS 92 ms and a similarly prolonged QT (~477 ms, QTc ~532 ms); measured the same way the QTc change is under 60 ms, so no QTc change is flagged. 2021-01-18 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 120/min (RR 496-504 ms) with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR ~180 ms. QRS 96 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no conduction block. Axis +65 deg (normal). QT ~277 ms, QTc ~392 ms. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 108 ms, QTc ~398 ms) the rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged (QTc difference 6 ms).

2025-06-23 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 54/min, regular, with a clearly visible P wave in II/aVF beginning ~255 ms before the QRS: PR ~215 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 86 ms with an rSr' in V1 that is not wide enough for right bundle branch block and a tall R in V6. Axis +14 deg. QT ~398 ms, Bazett QTc ~379 ms. Prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) was sinus at 51/min with a PR of ~185 ms, QRS 88 ms and QTc ~359 ms: no bundle branch block change and QTc unchanged (20 ms); the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree block range.

2025-09-13 tracing. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: RR intervals range 288-580 ms in a chaotic pattern (RMSSD ~104 ms), with no organised P wave anywhere and a flat/fibrillatory baseline; mean ventricular rate ~152/min. 2025-11-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 73/min, regular, prominent upright P in II (0.25 mV) with PR ~165 ms. QRS 94 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +2 deg. 2024-09-17 tracing. Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order authored that day; previous haloperidol exposure was inpatient in early 2025). Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09 (104253928), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily (a new 2026-09-01 warfarin order was also generated). Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD - authorised to adjust warfarin under the standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily for a home INR of 3.4. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review. The home INR of 3.4 pre-dates and triggered the change and cannot satisfy it.

80-year-old woman (born 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented repeatedly in cardiology clinic notes through 2026-06-22. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110, combined systolic/diastolic CHF I5040/I5043), hypertension (I10/4019), age >=75 (2), diabetes mellitus (E119/E11649, on insulin and oral agents), prior stroke/TIA (2 - personal history of TIA/cerebral infarction V1254 and hemiplegia following cerebral infarction I69351), vascular disease (atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery I2510, old myocardial infarction), female sex. There is no anticoagulant on the current medication list - only aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin - and aspirin monotherapy is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Oral anticoagulation is a Class 1 recommendation and should be started unless a contraindication is documented.

71-year-old man (born 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission and carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note through 2026-06-27. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). Score >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but the current medication list contains no anticoagulant (levothyroxine only; INRs around the 2025 admission were 1.1-1.6, consistent with no warfarin). Note the coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' from the same 2025 admission - bleeding risk should be reviewed, but it does not by itself preclude anticoagulation, so this needs a prescriber decision.

71-year-old woman (born 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 2025-03-14, the admission at which she also had cerebral infarction due to embolism (I6340/I639) with residual hemiplegia. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior stroke (2), hypertension (I10/4019, hypertensive CKD I129), age 65-74 (1), female sex (1). Her most recent ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with a PAC, consistent with paroxysmal AF - paroxysmal AF carries the same anticoagulation indication as persistent AF. The current medication list (famotidine, levothyroxine, metoprolol tartrate) contains no anticoagulant and no antithrombotic at all, despite a cardioembolic stroke. Oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated (Class 1).

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is a current order (authored 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04). The outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant was nonetheless re-ordered on 2026-08-20 and no documented cardiology review of the bleed is in the chart, so continuation of apixaban after a major GI bleed needs prescriber review (site treated? PPI? resume vs. switch?). Note the patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk.

48-year-old man (born 1978-02-27) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-07-19 to 2026-08-04 (and 'other specified cardiac dysrhythmias' coded 2025-06-17). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: congestive heart failure (congestive heart failure 4280, acute systolic heart failure 42821 and other primary cardiomyopathies 4254, coded 2025-02-26) plus hypertension (4019/40390). A score of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation. His chart even carries 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' (V5861, 2025-06-17), yet no anticoagulant appears on the current medication list (famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline). Anticoagulation status needs clarification and, if genuinely absent, initiation.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at that encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the note needs correction and the rapid AF needs management review.

Most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT ~490 ms and Bazett QTc ~524 ms, which is >=500 ms and therefore requires prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. The patient has been on escitalopram 10 mg daily continuously since 2024-05-14, with a current order authored 2026-07-18 (valid to 2026-12-26). Most recent electrolytes (2026-03-18) are acceptable: potassium 3.8 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. A repeat ECG on therapy and review of the need for escitalopram are warranted.

Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT ~540 ms and Bazett QTc ~546 ms (>=500 ms), which requires prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (authored 2026-07-12, valid to 2027-01-09) and had been restarted two weeks before that ECG. QTc rose from 424 ms on the prior tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07) to 546 ms after amiodarone was restarted. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so electrolytes do not explain the prolongation.

Most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT ~490 ms and Bazett QTc ~532 ms (>=500 ms), triggering prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. Citalopram 40 mg daily is a current order (authored 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07) and has been refilled continuously since 2023-10-02; 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum recommended when QT prolongation is a concern. Most recent potassium is 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and the most recent magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08), both normal. Dose reduction/alternative agent and a repeat ECG should be considered.

Most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT ~580 ms and Bazett QTc ~571 ms (>=500 ms), requiring prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (authored 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06) and has been continuous outpatient therapy. QTc rose from 467 ms on the prior tracing (100867733, 2022-04-06, atrial fibrillation) to 571 ms after conversion on amiodarone. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17) are normal. This 95-year-old also takes warfarin and metoprolol; an up-to-date ECG and review of continued amiodarone are needed.

Amiodarone (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (it was absent from the medication list at the 2025-09-21 visit and the previous amiodarone course had ended 2025-01-26). Under the 9/1/2025 memo an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG did show QTc ~546 ms, handled as a separate QT safety item).

The start pre-dates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. Oral anticoagulation is a Class 1 recommendation and should be started unless a contraindication is documented.

Note the coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' from the same 2025 admission - bleeding risk should be reviewed, but it does not by itself preclude anticoagulation, so this needs a prescriber decision.

The current medication list (famotidine, levothyroxine, metoprolol tartrate) contains no anticoagulant and no antithrombotic at all, despite a cardioembolic stroke. Oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated (Class 1).

PPI? resume vs. switch?). Note the patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk.

2025-12-25 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR ~830 ms), upright P in II with PR ~132 ms. QRS 88 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +20 deg. QT ~380 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. 2025-08-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, regular (RR ~720 ms), upright P in II with PR ~136 ms. QRS 78 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +55 deg. QT ~341 ms, Bazett QTc ~402 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2025-09-13 tracing. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: RR intervals range 288-580 ms in a chaotic pattern (RMSSD ~104 ms), with no organised P wave anywhere and a flat/fibrillatory baseline; mean ventricular rate ~152/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis -15 deg. QT ~255 ms, Bazett QTc ~407 ms. The prior ECG 107374881 (2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at ~77/min (regular RR ~780 ms apart from one ectopic beat) with a small but definite P wave and PR ~150 ms, QTc ~409 ms. Atrial fibrillation is therefore new; QTc is unchanged.

2025-11-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 73/min, regular, prominent upright P in II (0.25 mV) with PR ~165 ms. QRS 94 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +2 deg. QT ~356 ms, Bazett QTc ~394 ms. The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was also sinus rhythm (67/min, QRS 92 ms) but with a much longer QT (~500 ms, QTc ~528 ms); the QTc has fallen by ~134 ms (>=60 ms). This tracing confirms the same-day note 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'.

2025-02-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 74/min, regular (RR ~810 ms), well-formed upright P in II with PR ~176 ms (normal, below the 200 ms first-degree block threshold). QRS 92 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis +66 deg. QT ~378 ms, Bazett QTc ~420 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2023-06-26 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 112/min, strictly regular (RR 536-542 ms), with a single well-formed upright P wave in II (0.19 mV) per cycle beginning ~200 ms before the QRS: PR ~160 ms, 1:1 atrial-ventricular relationship, i.e. not atrial flutter despite the flutter coded elsewhere in the chart. QRS 98 ms with a very deep S in V1 (-3.0 mV) and tall R in I/V6 - LVH voltage, no bundle branch block. Axis +31 deg. QT ~294 ms, Bazett QTc ~401 ms. Prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) was identical in rhythm and conduction (sinus 115/min, QRS 96 ms, QTc ~393 ms): no change.

2025-03-14 tracing. Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min: the RR intervals are ~980 ms apart from a single early beat (538 ms) with a compensatory pause (1372 ms), i.e. one atrial ectopic, and a broad low-amplitude upright P wave precedes each sinus QRS starting ~250 ms before it - PR ~205 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. This is not atrial fibrillation, which fits the 'paroxysmal' atrial fibrillation coded at this encounter. QRS 100 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -33 deg (left axis deviation). QT ~390 ms, Bazett QTc ~394 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2026-04-29 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 69/min, regular (RR ~870 ms), upright P in II with PR ~134 ms. QRS 94 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. The QRS is deeply negative in I (S -1.3 mV) with a negative net aVF, giving a frontal axis of about -171 deg (extreme axis deviation). QT ~353 ms, Bazett QTc ~380 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2023-11-10 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, upright P in II with PR ~144 ms. QRS 102 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis +41 deg. Repolarisation is prolonged: QT ~490 ms, Bazett QTc ~532 ms. The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) showed sinus tachycardia at 132/min with QRS 96 ms and QTc ~436 ms; QTc has increased by ~96 ms (>=60 ms). The patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug - flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2026-03-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular (RR ~880 ms), upright P in II with PR ~144 ms. QRS 88 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Axis +44 deg. The T wave is biphasic (negative then positive in V5/II) and ends late: QT ~440-450 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 470 ms - prolonged but below the 500 ms threshold that would mandate prescriber review, so no QT safety item was raised. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. This is the post-start ECG for escitalopram begun 2026-02-12.

2019-01-13 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular, upright P in II (0.23 mV) with PR ~168 ms. QRS 92 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis about -14 deg (normal). QT ~382 ms, Bazett QTc ~359 ms. Prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) was sinus at 66/min with PR ~190 ms, QRS 106 ms and QTc ~390 ms: no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (31 ms).

2023-10-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, upright P in II, PR ~130 ms, QRS 92 ms (rS V1, tall R V6, no BBB), axis +35 deg. The T wave is markedly prolonged: QT ~490 ms, Bazett QTc ~524 ms. Prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) had identical rhythm/conduction but QT ~325 ms and QTc ~364 ms, so QTc has increased by ~160 ms (>=60 ms). The patient is on escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug - flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2022-07-13 tracing. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141/min (RR 404-454 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02). No sinus P wave: the deflection 170 ms before each QRS is negative in II, III and aVF and positive in V1 - the classic typical (counter-clockwise) flutter wave vector - and recurs at ~210 ms intervals, i.e. an atrial rate of ~280/min conducted 2:1, with the alternate flutter wave buried in the QRS. For comparison, this patient's sinus tracings show an upright 0.08 mV P wave in II, which is absent here. No measurable PR interval in flutter. QRS 86 ms - no bundle branch block. Axis -7 deg. QT ~280 ms, Bazett QTc ~429 ms. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) was atrial fibrillation (RR 380-822 ms, RMSSD ~190 ms, no organised atrial activity) at ~110/min with QTc ~432 ms, so the atrial fibrillation has organised into atrial flutter; QTc unchanged. No pacing spikes are seen despite the documented pacemaker.

2025-05-12 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 82/min, regular (RR ~730 ms), upright P in II with PR ~138 ms. QRS 104 ms - slightly widened but below 120 ms and without an rSR' in V1 or a broad monophasic R in V6, so no bundle branch block. Axis +28 deg. QT ~371 ms, Bazett QTc ~435 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

2022-07-16 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 91/min, regular, upright P in II with PR ~154 ms. QRS 82 ms - narrow, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -52 deg (left axis deviation, qR in I with rS in II/III/aVF). QT ~337 ms, Bazett QTc ~415 ms. Prior ECG 102616671 (2021-05-16) was sinus at 87/min, QRS 86 ms, QTc ~397 ms with a +21 deg axis: rhythm, conduction and QTc unchanged (18 ms); only the frontal axis has shifted leftward.

2024-07-17 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 61/min with a broad P wave in II starting ~275 ms before the QRS: PR ~210 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS is wide at 134 ms with a deep, slurred QS/rS complex in V1 (nadir -1.4 mV) and a broad notched monophasic R in I and V6 peaking late (~120 ms after QRS onset) with no S wave - left bundle branch block. Prior ECG 103686933 (2024-06-03) showed the same pattern (sinus 68/min, PR ~212 ms, QRS 132 ms LBBB, QTc ~462 ms), so there is no new or resolved block and no QTc change.

2024-04-19 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121/min (RR 492-500 ms), upright P in II/aVF before every QRS, PR ~125 ms. QRS 86 ms with rS in V1 and tall R in V6 - no bundle branch block. Axis +68 deg (normal). QT ~296 ms, Bazett QTc ~421 ms (upper normal, largely a consequence of Bazett over-correction at this rate). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior for comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, regular, upright P in II with PR ~130 ms. QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 (-1.07 mV) with tall R in V6 - voltage criteria only, no BBB. Axis +54 deg. QT ~317 ms, QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier and is essentially identical (101/min, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~409 ms): no change.

2024-10-24 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), broad low-amplitude but consistent P wave in II, PR ~160 ms. QRS 92 ms with rS in V1 and very tall R in V6 (3.3 mV, LVH voltage). Axis +34 deg. QT ~430 ms, QTc ~401 ms. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) showed sinus rhythm 57/min with one ectopic beat, QRS 90 ms, QTc ~404 ms - no interval or rhythm change. Of note, sinus rhythm here despite atrial fibrillation and Mobitz II being coded at this encounter; no AV block is evident on this tracing.

2024-12-05 14:38 tracing. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121/min (RR 492-496 ms), P wave before each QRS, PR ~100 ms. QRS is now narrow at 98 ms. The QRS is predominantly negative in I with an almost isoelectric, slightly negative aVF, giving a frontal axis of about -178 deg (extreme axis deviation). QT ~296 ms, QTc ~421 ms. The prior ECG 106516875 from earlier the same day (01:33) showed a QRS of ~150-158 ms with an rSR' pattern and a tall late R in V1 (1.14 mV peaking 114 ms after QRS onset) plus broad terminal S in I/V6 - right bundle branch block, matching the RBBB coded that day. That block has resolved on the later tracing (QTc 476 -> 421 ms, a 55 ms fall, below the 60 ms threshold).
