Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT ~540 ms, Bazett QTc ~546 ms. Prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) showed sinus rhythm with sinus arrhythmia at 47/min, QRS 100 ms, QT ~478 ms and QTc ~424 ms; QTc has therefore risen by ~120 ms (>=60 ms), coinciding with amiodarone being restarted on 2025-11-10. Flagged separately as a QT safety item.

2024-09-17 tracing. Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 386-1070 ms, RMSSD ~254 ms) with no organised or reproducible P wave in any lead, mean ventricular rate ~99/min. Because there is no atrial activity, no PR interval is measurable. QRS 84 ms - no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -63 deg (left axis deviation). QT ~324 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; atrial fibrillation was coded at the preceding day's encounter.

items.explanation: Two overlapping current oral anticoagulant orders: apixaban 5 mg BID (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic note documents switching from rivaroxaban to apixaban and starting apixaban, but rivaroxaban was never stopped; the same note still lists both drugs as current. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban confers a high bleeding risk and requires immediate reconciliation.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (absent from the medication list on 2025-12-15, first order authored 2026-03-02). Because the start was on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met (sinus rhythm, QTc ~380 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (first order and first appearance in the medication list). The start is on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. No ECG was obtained inside that window; the only tracing in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and five days after the deadline, so the required monitoring was not completed in time and the due date has passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was restarted at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (it was not on the medication list at the 2026-02-18 visit and the prior inpatient course ended 2026-01-01). The start is on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was restarted at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 after a long gap (previous course ended 2024-09-18). An ECG was therefore required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18, within the required window; the report was requested by fax but has not been received. That outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order authored that day; previous haloperidol exposure was inpatient in early 2025). Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09 (104253928), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr. Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily (a new 2026-09-01 warfarin order was also generated). Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD - authorised to adjust warfarin under the standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily for a home INR of 3.4. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the follow-up is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review. The home INR of 3.4 pre-dates and triggered the change and cannot satisfy it.

80-year-old woman (born 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented repeatedly in cardiology clinic notes through 2026-06-22. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110, combined systolic/diastolic CHF I5040/I5043), hypertension (I10/4019), age >=75 (2), diabetes mellitus (E119/E11649, on insulin and oral agents), prior stroke/TIA (2 - personal history of TIA/cerebral infarction V1254 and hemiplegia following cerebral infarction I69351), vascular disease (atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery I2510, old myocardial infarction), female sex. There is no anticoagulant on the current medication list - only aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin - and aspirin monotherapy is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Oral anticoagulation is a Class 1 recommendation and should be started unless a contraindication is documented.

71-year-old man (born 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission and carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note through 2026-06-27. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). Score >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but the current medication list contains no anticoagulant (levothyroxine only; INRs around the 2025 admission were 1.1-1.6, consistent with no warfarin). Note the coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' from the same 2025 admission - bleeding risk should be reviewed, but it does not by itself preclude anticoagulation, so this needs a prescriber decision.

71-year-old woman (born 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 2025-03-14, the admission at which she also had cerebral infarction due to embolism (I6340/I639) with residual hemiplegia. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior stroke (2), hypertension (I10/4019, hypertensive CKD I129), age 65-74 (1), female sex (1). Her most recent ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with a PAC, consistent with paroxysmal AF - paroxysmal AF carries the same anticoagulation indication as persistent AF. The current medication list (famotidine, levothyroxine, metoprolol tartrate) contains no anticoagulant and no antithrombotic at all, despite a cardioembolic stroke. Oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated (Class 1).

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is a current order (authored 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04). The outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant was nonetheless re-ordered on 2026-08-20 and no documented cardiology review of the bleed is in the chart, so continuation of apixaban after a major GI bleed needs prescriber review (site treated? PPI? resume vs. switch?). Note the patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk.

48-year-old man (born 1978-02-27) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-07-19 to 2026-08-04 (and 'other specified cardiac dysrhythmias' coded 2025-06-17). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: congestive heart failure (congestive heart failure 4280, acute systolic heart failure 42821 and other primary cardiomyopathies 4254, coded 2025-02-26) plus hypertension (4019/40390). A score of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation. His chart even carries 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' (V5861, 2025-06-17), yet no anticoagulant appears on the current medication list (famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline). Anticoagulation status needs clarification and, if genuinely absent, initiation.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at that encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the note needs correction and the rapid AF needs management review.

Most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT ~490 ms and Bazett QTc ~524 ms, which is >=500 ms and therefore requires prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. The patient has been on escitalopram 10 mg daily continuously since 2024-05-14, with a current order authored 2026-07-18 (valid to 2026-12-26). Most recent electrolytes (2026-03-18) are acceptable: potassium 3.8 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. A repeat ECG on therapy and review of the need for escitalopram are warranted.

Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT ~540 ms and Bazett QTc ~546 ms (>=500 ms), which requires prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (authored 2026-07-12, valid to 2027-01-09) and had been restarted two weeks before that ECG. QTc rose from 424 ms on the prior tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07) to 546 ms after amiodarone was restarted. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so electrolytes do not explain the prolongation.

Most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT ~490 ms and Bazett QTc ~532 ms (>=500 ms), triggering prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. Citalopram 40 mg daily is a current order (authored 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07) and has been refilled continuously since 2023-10-02; 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum recommended when QT prolongation is a concern. Most recent potassium is 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and the most recent magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08), both normal. Dose reduction/alternative agent and a repeat ECG should be considered.

Most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT ~580 ms and Bazett QTc ~571 ms (>=500 ms), requiring prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (authored 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06) and has been continuous outpatient therapy. QTc rose from 467 ms on the prior tracing (100867733, 2022-04-06, atrial fibrillation) to 571 ms after conversion on amiodarone. 80-year-old woman (born 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented repeatedly in cardiology clinic notes through 2026-06-22. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure I110, combined systolic/diastolic CHF I5040/I5043), hypertension (I10/4019), age >=75 (2), diabetes mellitus (E119/E11649, on insulin and oral agents), prior stroke/TIA (2 - personal history of TIA/cerebral infarction V1254 and hemiplegia following cerebral infarction I69351), vascular disease (atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery I2510, old myocardial infarction), female sex. There is no anticoagulant on the current medication list - only aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin - and aspirin monotherapy is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Oral anticoagulation is a Class 1 recommendation and should be started unless a contraindication is documented.

71-year-old man (born 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 admission and carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note through 2026-06-27. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (4019), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 41401). Score >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but the current medication list contains no anticoagulant (levothyroxine only; INRs around the 2025 admission were 1.1-1.6, consistent with no warfarin). Note the coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' from the same 2025 admission - bleeding risk should be reviewed, but it does not by itself preclude anticoagulation, so this needs a prescriber decision.

71-year-old woman (born 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 2025-03-14, the admission at which she also had cerebral infarction due to embolism (I6340/I639) with residual hemiplegia. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior stroke (2), hypertension (I10/4019, hypertensive CKD I129), age 65-74 (1), female sex (1). Her most recent ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with a PAC, consistent with paroxysmal AF - paroxysmal AF carries the same anticoagulation indication as persistent AF. The current medication list (famotidine, levothyroxine, metoprolol tartrate) contains no anticoagulant and no antithrombotic at all, despite a cardioembolic stroke. Oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated (Class 1).

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is a current order (authored 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04). The outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant was nonetheless re-ordered on 2026-08-20 and no documented cardiology review of the bleed is in the chart, so continuation of apixaban after a major GI bleed needs prescriber review (site treated? PPI? resume vs. switch?). Note the patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk.

48-year-old man (born 1978-02-27) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-07-19 to 2026-08-04 (and 'other specified cardiac dysrhythmias' coded 2025-06-17). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: congestive heart failure (congestive heart failure 4280, acute systolic heart failure 42821 and other primary cardiomyopathies 4254, coded 2025-02-26) plus hypertension (4019/40390). A score of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation. His chart even carries 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' (V5861, 2025-06-17), yet no anticoagulant appears on the current medication list (famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline). Anticoagulation status needs clarification and, if genuinely absent, initiation.

Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and atrial fibrillation was in fact coded at that encounter. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the note needs correction and the rapid AF needs management review.

Most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT ~490 ms and Bazett QTc ~524 ms, which is >=500 ms and therefore requires prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. The patient has been on escitalopram 10 mg daily continuously since 2024-05-14, with a current order authored 2026-07-18 (valid to 2026-12-26). Most recent electrolytes (2026-03-18) are acceptable: potassium 3.8 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, so the prolongation is not explained by hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia. A repeat ECG on therapy and review of the need for escitalopram are warranted.

Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT ~540 ms and Bazett QTc ~546 ms (>=500 ms), which requires prescriber review under the clinic QT monitoring memo. Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (authored 2026-07-12, valid to 2027-01-09) and had been restarted two weeks before that ECG. QTc rose from 424 ms on the prior tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07) to 546 ms after amiodarone was restarted. The current medication list (famotidine, levothyroxine, metoprolol tartrate) contains no anticoagulant and no antithrombotic at all, despite a cardioembolic stroke. Oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated (Class 1).

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is a current order (authored 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04). PPI? resume vs. switch?). Note the patient is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk.
